newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Reed Elsevier expands in U.S..
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Reed Elsevier expands in U.S..

text.p: Reed Elsevier, announcing its third U.S. acquisition this year, said on Monday it would spend $447 million of its own cash to buy U.S. trade magazine publisher Chilton Business Group from Walt Disney Co's ABC.
The Anglo-Dutch publishing group said the deal would make an immediate contribution to its profits.
Earlier this year Reed Elsevier acquired 40 U.S. law publications from Thomson Corp and its science publishing division bought MDL Information Systems Inc. for $320 million.
Despite these and other takeovers over the last year Reed Elsevier executives stressed that the group would continue to pursue an active aquisitions policy.
Chilton, based in Radnor Pennsylvania, made a pre-tax profit of $28 million in 1996 on sales of $203 million. Since 1992, it has achieved compound pre-tax profit growth of 17 percent.
Chilton publishes 39 business magazine titles, focusing on manufacturing, entertainment and automotive topics.
Reed-Elsevier said it would merge Chilton's core trade press business with its own U.S. business magazines unit, Cahners Publishing Co, which has a stable of over 90 titles.
It quoted its co-chairman Nigel Stapleton as saying Chilton was an ideal match for Cahners.
"Chilton fits superbly...and this acquisition offers attractive opportunities for revenue growth and operational synergies," Stapleton said.

Group strategy director Peter van Hooff told Reuters that by combining Chilton and Cahners, Reed-Elsevier could raise its U.S. business publishing operating profit margins to around 20 percent in 1999 from some 15 to 17 percent now.
Van Hooff said the deal would significantly strengthen Reed Elsevier's U.S. trade magazine publishing business, providing plenty of scope to raise revenues and cut costs.
Reed Elsevier would also be able to write off 80 to 90 percent of the purchase price against U.S. taxes over 15 years.
"The combination of Cahners and Chilton gives us even stronger positions in more markets," he said.
Van Hooff said Reed-Elsevier would eliminate overlap between previously competing titles and make them more complementary.

Chilton's magazines would also broaden and deepen the editorial content which Reed-Elsevier was able to offer via electronic media, he said, noting that Chilton did not previously have its own electronic publishing infrastructure.
"The Chilton titles will really benefit from the lead we have in electronic publishing," he said.

Van Hooff said Reed-Elsevier, which owns leading U.S. showbiz newspaper Variety, had already been planning an online information service for the entertainment industry and that the Chilton deal would add further momentum to this project.
Reed Elsevier's chief financial officer (CFO) Mark Armour said the group remained very lightly geared and still had plenty of financial scope for further takeovers.
"It should be absolutely clear that acquisitions are a constant activity for Reed Elsevier. We devote great energy to exploring opportunities and shaking the trees," he said.
Analysts generally welcomed the Chilton buy, saying it was a good fit with Cahners but not a major strategic move.
"This is a nice build-on acquisition, it can be integrated nicely and has obvious tax advantages," said Jeff Meys of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
The stock market's response was also fairly muted. In Amsterdam Elsevier shares were off 0.30 at 32.40 guilders, in London Reed was up 1.5 pence at 573.5.
